component.name: MavPlayer
component.summary: Play videos, music, streams and DVDs

description.p: MavPlayer is a fast, native media player. It opens almost any video or audio format, plays network streams and DVDs, and starts in a fraction of a second.

ul.li: Hardware-accelerated decoding with automatic software fallback
HDR to SDR tone mapping, deinterlacing, aspect ratio, crop, zoom and rotation
Embedded and external subtitles, with automatic loading of matching files
DVD playback with interactive disc menus, or straight to the main feature
Audio CDs and CD images, with track names from CD-Text
10-band equalizer, volume normalization, night mode and pitch-preserving speed control
Playlists, shuffle, repeat, A-B loop and resume where you left off

description.p: Play in the background: closing the window while a file is open hides it in the tray and playback goes on, with Play/Pause, Previous and Next in the tray icon's menu.
A Bicubic upscaler that needs no libplacebo, cover art upscaled from the original picture, tidier menus, an option to play playlist entries on a double click, and dragging the window by its video.

Seeking to nearby keyframes respects the direction, fullscreen controls hide when the cursor leaves the window, and memory leaks found by profiling are fixed: playlist cycling and long DVD or PGS subtitle playback no longer grow.

With NVIDIA GPUs, video is resized and converted on the GPU and copied out once at window size: playing 1080p60 in a window takes a fraction of the CPU it did, including AV1 and 10-bit H.264 that the GPU can't decode.

Much less memory: lean hardware decoders, smaller CUDA contexts, video memory that is reused or freed, and GPU devices that close when nothing plays. A new video frame no longer redraws the whole window.

DVD menus whose music ends before their animation no longer stall, Open Disc lists DVD titles faster, and the drive stays open between uses so the disc isn't read again. Menus and dialogs block the mouse from reaching what is behind them.
DVD menus: DVDs start at the disc's own menu, with buttons that work with the keyboard and the mouse, and play what the disc chooses next. Or play the main feature straight away.
Audio CDs, from a drive or a .cue/.bin image, with track names from CD-Text and gapless playback.
Big video frame buffers are reused instead of being allocated for every frame, and the Arch package builds again with CachyOS's default compiler flags.
Optionally keep running in the system tray, so files open in a warm window almost instantly, and hardware decoding starts much sooner.
Rebindable keyboard shortcuts in Preferences, smarter subtitle and audio track choice, the playlist in fullscreen, and scrollbars on menus, the playlist and dialogs.
GPU upscaling with Anime4K, FSRCNNX, ArtCNN, RAVU, AMD FSR, NVIDIA Image Scaling or your own mpv shader, plus KrigBilateral chroma and AMD CAS sharpening.
Native PipeWire audio on Linux, media keys and desktop player controls, opening files in the running window, and faster startup.
